- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥ 0.67) over recent days, model tends to underpredict; adjust forecast upward by 1–2% of recent mean.
- When sentiment is negative (≤ -0.33) or volatile, model often overpredicts; reduce forecast by 1–3% to align with mean reversion bias.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., +5%+ in 3–5 days), model frequently overshoots; cap forecast peak at 10–15% above recent high, then apply gradual decay.
- If sentiment shifts from negative to positive mid-horizon, model often fails to catch momentum; add 0.5–1.5% upward adjustment in second half of forecast.
- Model underperforms in 30-day horizon when sentiment is neutral (0.00–0.33); apply 1–2% upward bias to compensate for mean reversion lag.
- If last 3–5 days show strong upward sentiment but model forecast is flat or declining, force a 1–2% upward correction to avoid missing momentum.
